_meta.note: Curated offline subset of the MITRE ATLAS matrix (adversarial threats to ML, LLM, and agentic AI systems). Use `ouroboros-tool atlas sync --from <ATLAS.yaml>` to rebuild from upstream mitre-atlas/atlas-data.

techniques.name: Search for Victim's Publicly Available Research Materials
techniques.description: Adversaries gather papers, blog posts, and documentation describing the victim's AI/ML architecture.

techniques.name: Search for Publicly Available Adversarial Vulnerability Analysis
techniques.description: Adversaries search public vulnerability disclosures and jailbreak repositories targeting the model family.

techniques.name: Acquire Public ML Artifacts
techniques.description: Adversaries obtain public pretrained weights, tokenizers, or benchmark datasets to craft attacks.

techniques.name: Create Proxy ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries train or fine-tune a surrogate model to develop transferable adversarial inputs.

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries probe exposed AI endpoints to map supported models, tools, and guardrails.

techniques.name: Discover ML Artifacts
techniques.description: Adversaries locate model weights, embeddings, prompts, or datasets on compromised systems.

techniques.name: ML Supply Chain Compromise
techniques.description: Adversaries tamper with upstream models, packages, MCP servers, or datasets used by the AI system.

techniques.name: GPU Hardware
techniques.description: Compromise of accelerator hardware or firmware in the ML supply chain.

techniques.name: ML Software
techniques.description: Compromise of ML libraries, frameworks, plugins, or serialization loaders.

techniques.name: Data
techniques.description: Compromise of third-party training, fine-tuning, or retrieval datasets.

techniques.name: Model
techniques.description: Compromise of pretrained or hosted foundation models in the supply chain.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries rely on a user opening or passing untrusted artifacts to an AI system.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse legitimate API keys or user credentials to access AI services.

techniques.name: Discover ML Model Ontology
techniques.description: Adversaries probe label spaces, schemas, or supported output categories of a model.

techniques.name: Discover ML Model Family
techniques.description: Adversaries identify the underlying architecture or foundation model family.

techniques.name: Evade ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries alter inputs so classifiers, guardrails, or detectors misclassify them.

techniques.name: Backdoor ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries embed hidden trigger behaviors into model weights or fine-tuned adapters.

techniques.name: Poison ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries modify model weights or training runs to introduce a backdoor.

techniques.name: Inject Payload
techniques.description: Adversaries embed executable code or malicious deserialization payloads inside model files.

techniques.name: Publish Poisoned Datasets
techniques.description: Adversaries host manipulated datasets online expecting victims to ingest them.

techniques.name: Poison Training Data
techniques.description: Adversaries corrupt training or fine-tuning corpora to degrade integrity or implant triggers.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via ML Inference API
techniques.description: Adversaries infer sensitive training data or proprietary model properties via API queries.

techniques.name: Infer Training Data Membership
techniques.description: Adversaries determine whether specific records were present in the training set.

techniques.name: Invert ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries reconstruct representative training examples from model outputs.

techniques.name: Extract ML Model
techniques.description: Adversaries query an inference API to functionally replicate a proprietary model.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via Cyber Means
techniques.description: Adversaries steal AI artifacts or conversation logs using traditional network exfiltration.

techniques.name: Denial of ML Service
techniques.description: Adversaries flood or craft degenerate inputs to exhaust model compute or availability.

techniques.name: Erode ML Model Integrity
techniques.description: Adversaries degrade accuracy, calibration, or trustworthiness of an AI system over time.

techniques.name: Cost Harvesting
techniques.description: Adversaries trigger expensive token generation or compute loops to inflate victim costs.

techniques.name: ML Artifact Collection
techniques.description: Adversaries collect model checkpoints, prompts, or vector stores from the environment.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.description: Adversaries leverage AI connectors or RAG access to collect sensitive repository data.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Adversaries coerce an agent into reading sensitive local files or environment data.

techniques.name: ML Model Inference API Access
techniques.description: Adversaries interact with a target model solely through its exposed inference API.

techniques.name: Verify Attack
techniques.description: Adversaries validate crafted adversarial inputs against local or staging targets before deployment.

techniques.name: Craft Adversarial Data
techniques.description: Adversaries generate inputs designed to induce targeted misbehavior in an ML model.

techniques.name: White-Box Optimization
techniques.description: Adversaries use model gradients or internals to optimize adversarial inputs.

techniques.name: Black-Box Optimization
techniques.description: Adversaries iteratively query the target API to optimize adversarial inputs.

techniques.name: Black-Box Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries craft inputs on a proxy model and transfer them to the target.

techniques.name: Manual Modification
techniques.description: Adversaries manually iterate prompts or inputs to bypass filters and steer outputs.

techniques.name: Insert Backdoor Trigger
techniques.description: Adversaries embed a known trigger token or pattern into an input to activate a backdoor.

techniques.name: Full ML Model Access
techniques.description: Adversaries have white-box access to model weights, architecture, and hyperparameters.

techniques.name: Spamming ML System with Chaff Data
techniques.description: Adversaries flood an AI-assisted triage or detection pipeline with noise to hide real alerts.

techniques.name: ML-Enabled Product or Service
techniques.description: Adversaries access the AI model indirectly through a customer-facing product feature.

techniques.name: External Harms
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse an AI system to cause financial, reputational, user, or IP harms.

techniques.name: Financial Harm
techniques.description: AI system manipulation leading to unauthorized transactions or financial loss.

techniques.name: Reputational Harm
techniques.description: AI system manipulation producing defamatory or brand-damaging outputs.

techniques.name: Societal Harm
techniques.description: Abuse of AI outputs to cause broad misinformation or societal disruption.

techniques.name: User Harm
techniques.description: AI system manipulation resulting in unsafe advice, phishing, or harm to end users.

techniques.name: ML Intellectual Property Theft
techniques.description: Extraction of proprietary prompts, fine-tuned weights, or RAG knowledge.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities in web wrappers, APIs, or agent orchestration endpoints.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries coerce an LLM or agent into emitting or executing shell, Python, or OS commands.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries craft inputs that override system instructions or hijack an LLM agent's control flow.

techniques.name: Direct Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries supply adversarial instructions directly in the user prompt.

techniques.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries embed instructions inside untrusted documents, web pages, emails, or tool outputs.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversaries deliver malicious links or prompt-injection lures via email or messaging.

techniques.name: LLM Plugin Compromise
techniques.description: Adversaries hijack plugins, function calls, or MCP tools via poisoned descriptions or arguments.

techniques.name: LLM Jailbreak
techniques.description: Adversaries use persona framing, role-play, or policy bypasses to override model alignment.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.description: Adversaries extract API keys, secrets, or tokens embedded in prompts, code, or agent memory.

techniques.name: LLM Meta Prompt Extraction
techniques.description: Adversaries trick an LLM into revealing its hidden system prompt or developer instructions.

techniques.name: LLM Data Leakage
techniques.description: Adversaries cause an LLM to disclose confidential context, PII, or proprietary RAG data.

techniques.name: Publish Hallucinated Entities
techniques.description: Adversaries register package names or URLs frequently hallucinated by LLMs (slopsquatting).

techniques.name: Activation Triggers
techniques.description: Adversaries plant conditional instructions that activate only when specific keywords appear.

techniques.name: Publish Poisoned Models
techniques.description: Adversaries upload trojaned checkpoints or LoRAs to public model hubs.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Self-Replication
techniques.description: Adversaries craft self-propagating prompts that copy themselves across agent messages or memory.

techniques.name: Discover LLM System Information
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate model version, context window, or connected tools via probing.

techniques.name: Discover LLM Hallucinations
techniques.description: Adversaries probe an LLM to identify recurring fabricated packages, domains, or facts.

techniques.name: Gather RAG-Indexed Targets
techniques.description: Adversaries identify documents or data sources indexed into a victim's RAG pipeline.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Crafting
techniques.description: Adversaries develop and refine reusable injection templates and jailbreak wrappers.

techniques.name: Retrieval Content Crafting
techniques.description: Adversaries prepare external web pages, tickets, or documents containing hidden prompt injections.

techniques.name: LLM Trusted Output Components Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries spoof structured delimiters, citations, or tool-output markers to bypass trust boundaries.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
techniques.description: Adversaries encode, translate, or obfuscate prompts (base64, homoglyphs, zero-width) to evade filters.

techniques.name: Discover LLM System Configurations
techniques.description: Adversaries extract system prompts, tool schemas, or guardrail configurations.

techniques.name: System Prompt
techniques.description: Discovery of hidden system or developer instructions governing the model.

techniques.name: Tool Definitions
techniques.description: Discovery of available tools, MCP schemas, and parameter constraints.

techniques.name: Guardrails
techniques.description: Probing of content filters, moderation classifiers, and refusal triggers.

techniques.name: RAG Poisoning
techniques.description: Adversaries insert adversarial content into a vector store or knowledge base for later retrieval.

techniques.name: False RAG Entry Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries inject fabricated entries into RAG stores to skew retrieval ranking and answers.

techniques.name: LLM Response Rendering
techniques.description: Adversaries abuse Markdown images, links, or HTML rendered from LLM outputs to exfiltrate data or run scripts.

techniques.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning
techniques.description: Adversaries corrupt an agent's persistent memory or active conversation thread.

techniques.name: Memory
techniques.description: Poisoning of long-term agent memory stores across sessions.

techniques.name: Thread
techniques.description: Poisoning of the active multi-turn conversation thread or scratchpad.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
techniques.description: Adversaries steer an agent into calling outbound tools (email, HTTP, webhooks) with sensitive data.
